title: Proof: no engine beats Carnot's
summary: Suppose a super-engine X beat the Carnot engine. Run a reversed Carnot engine off its work: heat would flow cold → hot by itself. Impossible!
alt: Engine X, claimed more efficient than a Carnot engine, drives a reversed Carnot engine. The combined machine would move heat from the cold reservoir to the hot one with no work, which the second law forbids.

wall.label: Cylinder / axes
wall.text: Walls of the cylinder and the graph axes.

hot.label: Isothermal at T₁ (a→b)
hot.text: Heat Q₁ flows IN from the hot reservoir; T stays T₁.

cold.label: Isothermal at T₂ (c→d)
cold.text: Heat Q₂ flows OUT to the cold reservoir; T stays T₂.

work.label: Work
work.text: Work done by the gas (area under the curve / inside the loop).

adB.label: Engine X (claimed)
adB.text: No heat flows; the gas cools from T₁ to T₂.

ok.label: Reversed Carnot engine
ok.text: Allowed by the laws of physics.

steps.title: The claim
steps.text: Suppose someone builds an engine **X** between the same two reservoirs that is **more efficient** than a Carnot engine: \(\eta_X>\eta_C\). Here \(\eta_C=1-T_2/T_1={{ec*100|0}}\%\) and the claim is \(\eta_X={{ex|0}}\%\). We shall show this leads to an impossibility.

steps.title: Run engine X
steps.text: X takes \(Q_1={{Q1x|0}}\) J from the hot reservoir, turns \(\eta_X Q_1=W={{Wx|0}}\) J into work and dumps \(Q_2={{Q2x|0}}\) J into the cold one.

steps.title: Feed W to a reversed Carnot engine
steps.text: A Carnot engine is reversible, so we can run it **backwards** as a refrigerator. Give it that same work \(W={{Wx|0}}\) J. It takes \(Q_2={{Q2c|0}}\) J from the cold reservoir and delivers \(Q_1=W/\eta_C={{Q1c|0}}\) J to the hot one.

steps.title: Add up both machines
steps.text: Hot reservoir: gave \({{Q1x|0}}\) J and got back \({{Q1c|0}}\) J, a net gain of {{net|0}} J. Cold reservoir: lost the same amount. The work \(W\) went round inside and none is left over. The pair moves heat from cold to hot **with no work done on it**.

steps.title: The contradiction
steps.text: The second law says heat cannot flow from a colder to a hotter body by itself. So engine X cannot exist. Move the **claimed efficiency** slider below \(\eta_C\): the net heat becomes zero or negative and nothing is wrong. That is the real-engine case.

steps.title: The theorem
steps.text: **No engine working between two given temperatures is more efficient than a Carnot engine.** Swap the roles of two Carnot engines in the same argument and neither can beat the other, so **all** Carnot engines between \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) have the same efficiency \(1-T_2/T_1\), whatever the working substance.

formulas.title: Carnot's theorem
formulas.text: No engine between the same two reservoirs can beat the Carnot engine.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: The Carnot engine here has \(\eta_C=50\%\) (\(T_1=600\) K, \(T_2=300\) K). Someone claims \(\eta_X=60\%\). With \(Q_1=100\) J, how many joules of heat would flow from the cold to the hot reservoir by themselves?
challenges.hint: \(W=60\) J, so the reversed Carnot engine delivers \(60/0.5\) J to the hot side.
challenges.explain: \(W=60\) J; the reversed Carnot engine delivers \(Q_1=60/0.5=120\) J to the hot side; the net is \(120-100=20\) J.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: If engine X has \(\eta_X\) **less** than \(\eta_C\), what happens?

options.label: No contradiction; it is an ordinary (irreversible) engine
Heat flows cold → hot by itself

challenges.hint: Check the sign of the net heat in the slider.
challenges.explain: The net heat to the hot reservoir is then zero or negative, so no law is broken. Real engines are of this kind.

takeaways: A more efficient engine would let heat flow cold → hot with no work: forbidden.
All reversible engines between the same temperatures have the same efficiency.

notes.title: Second-law form used
notes.text: We use the statement that heat cannot flow from a colder to a hotter body without work being done. Check it against the wording in your book.
